about.title: Who we are
about.p1: We are a team of artists and educators formed in 2016 within the framework of the educational programmes of the Athens Epidaurus Festival. We design and deliver drama education programmes for children and adults, drawing inspiration from ancient drama as our starting point. Our experience at Epidaurus forms the foundation of our work, while we continually seek new ways to bring ancient drama closer to diverse audiences.
about.p2: Why ancient drama? Although its stories come from a distant world, the questions they raise remain relevant to us today and continue to resonate with contemporary life. This ongoing dialogue between past and present is what interests us and lies at the heart of our work. Through drama education, we aim to create a space where children and adults can engage with ancient drama, interpret it, and discover their own connections to it.

do.title: Discover what we do
do.intro: We design a «journey» through which children are gradually initiated, through individual activities, into the magical universe of each play.

do.outro: in a fun and interactive way. The children reflect on the questions the text raises and are called upon to make decisions about how the story unfolds.

collectiveSpace.title: Collective shaping of the space
collectiveSpace.text: The visual-arts part is always the beginning of the programme, as it introduces the children to the story through the making of set objects that carry symbolic value, conveying meanings about the action to follow.

teacherInRole.title: Teacher in role
teacherInRole.text: The facilitator chooses the role suited to each moment, using a representative feature of that role (an object, a characteristic gesture, and so on). This technique sparks the students' interest, fosters their emotional engagement and creates the conditions for social interaction among the members of the group.

collectiveRole.title: Collective role
collectiveRole.text: The children collectively play the role of a single character. Each child is free to speak whenever they feel they can add something to the role, without any need for agreement between their views. At a later stage of the technique, the children can jointly arrive at a collective portrayal of a role that they all agree on to some degree, which also strengthens cooperation.

hotSeating.title: Hot seating
hotSeating.text: A child, or a facilitator in role, is questioned by the rest of the group in order to bring to light the character's motives, actions, perceptions, values and so on. This technique is best used at a crucial moment of the drama and makes it easier to reach a decisive choice, as it helps the children study human behaviour in depth.

mantleExpert.title: Mantle of the expert
mantleExpert.text: Without realising it, the children «know» what they don't believe they know. As experts, they are asked to investigate the data they are given, to solve riddles and to piece together clues, so that the world of the myth unfolds before them — along with the central question on which they are each time asked to take a position.

conscienceAlley.title: Conscience alley
conscienceAlley.text: The group splits in two and forms two facing rows, creating an alley. A facilitator or a child playing a particular role walks down the alley, while the other children voice the character's thoughts or offer advice about a decision they need to make. The character walking the alley, having heard the «voices of their conscience», then acts accordingly.
